title: Bulguksa
visualBrief: Specific principal Bulguksa compound exterior: sixteen mapped halls/galleries and western auxiliary buildings, two courts, higher Birojeon/Gwaneumjeon/Nahanjeon, both entrance stone stair bridges, Dabotap, Seokgatap and the small sarira stupa. The large373m religious park boundary is not one building and remains outside this model.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q408318/way382655135 identifies the wider site. Sixteen actual normal-map roof footprints identify the principal halls and gallery arms; point controls17598413339131/17598413339130/17596588194605 place Dabotap, Seokgatap and the sarira stupa. The ordinary visitor-style layout guides names and relative courts, while current PMTiles geometry controls metric positions. Raw east/south coordinates retain the signed front approach; the main hall east axis is9.67 degrees north of east. Concave gallery roof ribbons are rectified within approximately55cm to suppress sub-metre map jitter; original control vertices remain unchanged in source.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Building wall/roof heights and courtyard levels are picture/DEM visualization estimates. Ordinary article heights10.4m Dabotap,8.2m Seokgatap and2.1m sarira stupa guide their nominal tops. Main entrance stairs use34 approximate risers split16/18; western stairs use17 split10/7. Roof curvature, brackets, panel bays, pagoda finial/body allocation, bridge arch and rail geometry are simplified estimates rather than surveys.

reconstruction.terrainBasis: Reviewed approximate full-site fit on the unchanged 161-square/6m standard DEM. Sixteen mapped halls retain raw east/south coordinates; the main hall east axis is9.67 degrees north of east and the stairs face the southern approach. Individual court levels step up the hillside. Twenty-seven occupied floor pockets merge to ten level meshes, each with a complete opaque top and continuous retaining foundation. Entrance bridge walks have inward cut-bank joins to the coarse DEM. First-render foundation gaps were corrected; the open stone vault remains real geometry. These buried joins and court/threshold levels are visualization estimates, not surveyed basement walls. Only bounded occupied floors open ground; sixteen individual guarded roof envelopes replace authored buildings. All115 independent source-map records were checked outside these envelopes. Full-site loading replaces16 authored roofs and preserves42 independent tile buildings exactly. Three native water features retain19263.106301357795 square metres. Failure keeps all58 native tile buildings and terrain; eviction restores surfaces and frees geometry. Synthetic64m residency clips the architecture, including part of the entrance bridge, and retains the existing temporary-boundary contact limitation. Partial architectural completeness/contact is not approved. Only the portable source preview seats terrain under authored floors; production uses the unmodified retained grid.

terrainReference.basis: The original161-square/6m standard Mapzen-USGS grid is retained with247.399m raw datum. Courtyard levels follow samples at the mapped halls and step up the hillside. Every bounded occupied court/foundation has an opaque top and sampled edge joins at every level. Only these occupied floors open terrain; surrounding paths, water and independent buildings remain native. The source preview seats terrain below authored floors solely for viewing. Exact archaeological threshold heights and canopy-influenced DEM levels are not surveyed.
